result.title: ViMoLa: Discrete Motion Tokens for Language-Guided Video Generation
result.summary: Language-guided video generation often captures scene content while missing the requested motion. We present ViMoLa (Video Motion Language), which predicts a motion prior from language and injects it into a frozen image-to-video backbone. A spatial vector-quantized autoencoder compresses dense trajectories into 64 tokens from a 512-entry codebook; a 28M-parameter transformer predicts the tokens from text; and zero-gated cross-attention adapters condition every frozen Wan~2.2 DiT block through forward hooks. Trained on 462K videos from Something-Something~v2 and Kinetics-400, ViMoLa raises directional accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442 (chance 0.250), with similar measured generative quality. Across-prompt shuffled codes achieve 0.283, supporting the importance of prompt-matched token content. A low-rank adapter reaches 0.428 at 1.45% additional forward-pass FLOPs, and reusing the tokenizer and language model with newly trained CogVideoX adapters raises accuracy from 0.301 to 0.398. Control remains imperfect: oracle codes reach 0.531, compound-motion gains are smaller, and the adapter does not explicitly preserve token-to-patch assignments.

AI.brief_summary: ViMoLa 用空间向量量化自编码器把稠密轨迹压成 64 个离散运动 token，由小型 transformer 从文本预测，再通过零门控 cross-attention 适配器注入冻结的图像到视频骨干，以补上语言指令中的运动信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「离散 token 瓶颈 + 从文本预测 + 注入冻结骨干」链路及打乱 token 的对照消融，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态如何生成、注入以及如何检验其内容是否被真正使用提供可核查的方法线索，但主题属视频生成而非 VLM 推理。
